Title: Malaysia has sufficient fuel supply despite Middle East tensions: Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia has secured sufficient fuel supply until the end of the year despite ongoing disruptions caused by tensions in the Middle East, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said the government has secured alternative fuel sources as part of contingency measures to mitigate risks arising from prolonged instability in the region, including disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz.
"So far, we have managed to secure the supply of fuel up until year-end.
"We have found alternative sources for fuel supply," he told reporters in a press conference at the OECD Economic Surveys: Malaysia 2026 here today.
Akmal said the government remained cautious and would continue to assess whether further interventions were needed to ensure supply sustainability while allowing economic activities to continue.
He added that Malaysia was also strengthening its energy resilience through measures such as increasing biodiesel blending, with the transition from B10 to B15 completed within two months.
Akmal also noted that the government currently had no plans to further phase out fuel subsidies beyond existing measures.
He said the government was focused on balancing two priorities, namely ensuring a stable fuel supply while keeping fuel affordable for consumers.
"The government has reduced the fuel allocation from 300 litres to 200 litres.
"So far, this is what the government has done. If there is anything else, the government will update the public," he said.
Separately, OECD director of the Country Studies Branch at the Economics Department Dr Luiz de Mello said Malaysia should gradually move away from broad-based fossil fuel subsidies and instead rely on targeted assistance for vulnerable households.
He said reducing subsidies would strengthen public finances while encouraging a more efficient transition away from fossil fuels.
"The reduction of the cap from 300 to 200 litres is a step in the right direction. It reduces the size of the subsidy and safeguards public finances," he said.
He added that Malaysia had stronger socioeconomic data capabilities that could support more targeted direct transfers to households that genuinely require assistance.
On Malaysia's economic outlook, de Mello said the country remained resilient despite global uncertainties, including geopolitical conflicts and policy uncertainty worldwide.
He said the OECD expects Malaysia's economy to grow by around five per cent on average this year and next year, supported by encouraging economic indicators.
However, he cautioned that as an open economy integrated into global value chains, Malaysia remained exposed to external shocks.
"The baseline scenario is for solid growth, but we are operating in a global landscape fraught with uncertainty," he said.

Title: Buntong tragedy: Families coping well after loss of two schoolgirls
Article:
IPOH: The families of the two schoolgirls who died in the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats tragedy in Buntong are coping well and do not require counselling at this stage.
State Women, Family, Social Welfare, Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Committee chairman Datuk Salbiah Mohamed said officers from the Social Welfare Department had visited and met the families following the tragedy, and found them to be in a stable condition despite their loss.
"Any family would find it difficult to accept the loss of a loved one, especially when it happens so suddenly. The grief is certainly there.
"However, following the department's engagement with the families, we found that they are in a stable and controlled condition.
"At the moment, there is no need for counselling because they are coping well," she told reporters after opening the Prismanita Open Day and Advocacy Programme on Women's Well-being @ Domestic Violence at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here today.
On Friday, two
14-year-old schoolgirls were found dead
after they were believed to have fallen from an upper floor of the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats near Buntong.
Asked whether the incident could have been linked to domestic violence, Salbiah said the matter should be left to the police as investigations were still ongoing.
"We do not know whether the incident was related to domestic violence or otherwise. I leave that to the police because the investigation is still ongoing.
"What we can do under my portfolio, through the Social Welfare Department, is to provide the necessary support to the families," she said.
Salbiah said the state government would continue strengthening community awareness and welfare programmes to help prevent similar incidents.
She said communities must play a more proactive role in identifying individuals or families who may be facing difficulties.
"We need to raise awareness and strengthen the role of the community so that people are more alert to what is happening around them.
"If there are signs that something is not right involving neighbours or members of the community, it should be reported. This is not about interfering in other people's affairs, but about preventing regret after something has happened," she said.
Salbiah said family and community well-being remained among the state's priorities under the Perak Sejahtera 2030 agenda, adding that development should not focus solely on physical infrastructure but also on the welfare of society.
"We will give greater focus to these aspects because the well-being of families and communities must be prioritised," she said.
On student-related issues, including bullying, Salbiah said the state government was also conducting advocacy programmes with the police's Sexual, Women and Child Investigation Division.
She said the state planned to discuss with Education, Higher Learning, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairuddin Abu Hanipah the possibility of establishing a committee to address child-related crimes and bullying as part of a comprehensive programme for students.
"We will look into the need to establish such a committee and involve our strategic partners to strengthen efforts to protect children and students," she said.

Title: Police reclassify toddler's death as murder, father to be charged
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU:  Police have reclassified the death of an 18-month-old boy as murder after nearly three years of investigation, with the child's biological father identified as the main suspect.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged by a doctor at the  Emergency Department of Hospital Sultan Ismail on Sept 13, 2023.
He said the child  was brought to the hospital, unconscious, by his 40-year-old father. An  examination found bruising on the waist, a bloated abdomen and swelling around  the anus.
"The victim  was pronounced dead at 10.40am the same day. Initially, the case was  investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 on suspicion of  neglect resulting in death," he said at a press conference at the Johor  police contingent headquarters today.
Ab Rahaman said  police interviewed 13 people, including the victim's immediate family members  and the family of his babysitter, and collected blood samples for  deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) analysis.
However, he said  the Chemistry Department was unable to identify a suspect because traces of  fluid believed to be semen found on the victim's anus were insufficient for  analysis and comparison.
"The  investigation continued, leading to the arrest of the victim's 40-year-old  biological father on July 18 and his 35-year-old uncle on July 22.
"Checks  found that the father, who worked as a labourer in Singapore, had no prior  criminal record, while the uncle had 13 criminal and drug-related records and  tested positive for cannabis in a urine screening test," he said.
He said the  latest findings did not rule out the possibility that the child had been  sodomised by his biological father, although investigations were ongoing.
Police also found  pornographic images and videos on the father's mobile phone, he said.
Following the  latest developments, the case has been reclassified under Section 302 of the  Penal Code for murder and Section 292 of the Penal Code for possession of  obscene material.
"The suspect  will be brought before the Johor Bahru Magistrate's Court tomorrow to face both  charges, while the victim's uncle, who has since been released, will be a  prosecution witness," he said.

Title: United Asiapac prices IPO at 35 sen ahead of Aug 19 debut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: United Asiapac Energy Bhd has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at 35 sen a share, seeking to raise RM48.73 million to support its expansion ahead of its ACE Market debut on Aug 19.
The IPO comprises 139.22 million new shares, giving the company an estimated market capitalisation of RM192.5 million based on the IPO price. Applications open today and close on Aug 5.
United Asiapac said nearly half of the proceeds would be used to acquire well intervention tools and equipment, with the balance allocated for a new corporate office, workforce expansion, engineer recruitment, repayment of borrowings, working capital and listing expenses.
The company provides well intervention services to upstream oil and gas operators throughout the lifecycle of hydrocarbon wells.
Its core services include fishing, which involves retrieving stuck or damaged downhole equipment, plug and abandonment to safely decommission wells, and sidetracking to access new production zones or bypass damaged sections of existing wells.
Managing director Ahmad Fadzuli Ali said the IPO would strengthen the company's operational capabilities as demand for well intervention services continued to grow.
He said the company's operational bases in Kemaman and Labuan enabled it to respond quickly to customers across Peninsular and East Malaysia, giving it an advantage over overseas service providers that rely on cross-border logistics.
He added that demand for the company's services has remained resilient despite heightened geopolitical uncertainty because well intervention work is driven by operators' need to maintain well integrity and meet regulatory requirements, rather than by new exploration activities.
United Asiapac has completed more than 200 projects since 2021.
For the nine-month financial period ended Sept 30, 2026, the company posted a gross profit of RM21.9 million, surpassing its full-year gross profit of RM14.5 million in the previous financial year. It attributed the stronger performance to sustained demand for its specialised services.
TA Securities Holdings Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari: Next Negri government must help plantations with replanting
Article:
JEMPOL: The next Negri Sembilan government must help oil palm plantations undergo replanting, says Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Johari said observations along the route to Felda Palong 3 showed that many existing oil palm trees were old.
"I was driving past earlier and saw many old oil palm trees.
"For us to maintain income from these oil palm plantations, replanting is essential.
"During Barisan Nasional's time, we carried out extensive replanting.
"Whoever forms the Negri Sembilan government must address the plantation issues in the state," he told reporters after visiting Felda Palong 3 with BN's Palong candidate Datuk Mustapha Nagoor.
Johari, a former plantation and commodities minister, said the incoming government must initiate replanting efforts to ensure a consistent income for settlers in the future.
"When oil palm trees become too old, we must figure out how to assist with replanting.
"Replanting ensures that settlers have a guaranteed income in the future," he said.

Title: Australia's sudden housing chill seeps into economy
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia's housing market is suffering its worst slowdown since the pandemic as rising borrowing costs and a sharp reversal in tax breaks shake confidence in a normally reliable source of economic growth.
Buyers and sellers alike have suddenly stepped back as house price appreciation no longer seems inevitable, a sea change in mood after decades of inexorable gains that turned Australian property into some of the world's most expensive.
With home prices in Sydney and Melbourne down nearly 5.0 per cent so far this year, the chill is evident in fewer people at open houses, tumbling auction clearance rates, a plunge in loan enquiries and a slump in property sales.
It's a sign of tougher conditions ahead for the broader economy, with real estate agents, removalists and tradespeople starting to see less work, while state governments brace for large write-downs in vital stamp-duty revenue. The New South Wales government in June cut its stamp-duty forecasts by A$5.3 billion (US$3.7 billion) over the next four years.
There is also the risk to consumer spending via the so-called wealth effect. With around two-thirds of Australian households owning their homes, rising property values have long anchored confidence to borrow and spend.
Jason Zhang, the 36-year-old owner of a kitchen renovation business in Sydney, said many clients were shelving new projects, making him worried that work will dry up next year.
"Unless interest rates come down, there won't be much change," he said. "Everyone is bracing for a long haul."
To be sure, the retreat in housing prices comes off an exceptionally high base. The total value of Australia's 11.5 million homes surged 87 per cent this decade to an unprecedented A$12.8 trillion.
It was also partly by design. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates three times between February and May to tame inflation fuelled by the Iran war, reversing the policy easing last year that had helped fuel record home prices.
"The housing market is a bit of a litmus test" for whether financial conditions are tight enough to bring inflation back down, RBA Governor Michele Bullock said on Tuesday.
"If it looks like that inflation is not coming down, then I think the board has some difficult decisions to make."
At the same time, "we have seen the housing market slow more than we were expecting," she said.
LOAN DEMAND PLUNGE
A government overhaul of investor tax breaks has added to the pressure by curbing negative gearing on established homes and scrapping a generous tax discount for investors.
Data from credit analytics firm Equifax showed mortgage inquiry levels dropped 14 per cent in June from a year earlier, marking a sharp reversal from January's growth of nearly 11 per cent.
Younger buyers with limited savings, who are more sensitive to rising rates, are driving the pullback. Research from property data provider Cotality showed higher borrowing costs mean properties have not become more affordable in Sydney and Melbourne despite the decline in housing prices.
"Even though the market drops and there are more accommodative government policies, a lot of first home buyers are hesitant to commit to a long-term liability," said Liza Cheong, a mortgage broker in Sydney.
"Investors who wanted to negatively gear just withdrew from their plans," she said. "The energy from clients is completely different from before."
That is a threat to the biggest single cash cow for Australia's banks as competition for borrowers heats up. The overall index of bank shares has tumbled 12 per cent since February, wiping more than A$60 billion from their market value.
The slowdown is reaching retailers too. Shares in department store Myer plunged 10 per cent on Monday after it warned of a consumer spending slump in June and July, citing "a weaker housing market" among the pressures on households.
New property listings are falling even as total housing stock climbs, a sign that homes are sitting unsold for longer. Sydney unit sales fell to just 2,495 in June, the lowest in at least five years barring the seasonal January lull, while open-home attendance dropped to an average of 2.1 people in the four weeks to July 11, according to real estate agency Ray White.
With oil prices staying high, bets on Reserve Bank policy easing next year have all but evaporated, dimming hopes for a quick housing market turnaround.
"We will get used to the new trading conditions and we'll resume business as usual at some point," said Sebastian Watkins, CEO at Lendi Group, Australia's largest retail mortgage broker.
"Is it six months? Is it 12 months? It's really hard to say."

Title: Bachok Amanah Youth chief claims trial to posting false info on fuel prices
Article:
SEPANG: Bachok Amanah Youth chief Abdullah Aqili Romeli pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court today to posting false information on petrol and diesel prices.
Abdullah Aqili, 35, who appeared as a summoned person, was accused of publishing the communication on the Threads platform under the account @qilieybrembo with the intention of annoying others at 12pm on March 31.
The post was viewed at 3pm on the same day at Tower 1 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) headquarters in Cyberjaya.
He was charged under Section 233(1)(a) of the MCMC Act 1998, punishable under Section 233(2) , which carries a fine of up to RM500,000 or a jail term of up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
The offence also carries an additional fine of RM5,000 for each day the offence continues after conviction.
He entered his plea before judge Ahmad Fuad Othman.
MCMC prosecuting officer Nur Nazhzilah Mohammad Hashim asked the court to set bail at RM10,000 with one surety and to impose additional conditions deemed appropriate.
Abdullah Aqili, who was unrepresented, appealed for lower bail, saying he worked as a mechanic and supported an adopted child.
"I came all the way from Kelantan today with RM300."
Ahmad Fuad set bail at RM7,000 with one surety and fixed Aug 26 for case mention and the appointment of a lawyer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gobind: Malaysia's AI ambition needs whole-of-nation push
Article:
CYBERJAYA: Malaysia must shift from a government-led approach to a whole-of-nation effort to achieve its ambition of becoming an artificial intelligence (AI) nation by 2030, says Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo.
He said the government established AI Malaysia as a platform to pool the expertise, resources and stakeholders required to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem.
He said the initiative would ensure discussions on AI development move beyond government policy to engage all affected sectors.
"We are now adopting a whole-of-nation approach as opposed to a whole-of-government approach.
"This means we need a place where all sectors involved can come together and discuss the challenges faced by different sectors," he said after launching AI Malaysia Berhad.
AI Malaysia is a new institution tasked with shaping national AI policy, establishing direction and driving effective implementation.
Previously, he said, Malaysia relied on a whole-of-government framework where ministries and agencies operated strictly within their respective mandates.
However, AI development demands broader collaboration involving universities, private companies, startups, data centre operators and technology providers.
"Academia will provide their views, the private sector will provide their input, and we will look at our local capacity, how we can develop startups and what we need in terms of data centres and computing power.
"It is a much broader conversation," he said.
Gobind said AI Malaysia was established following two years of engagement between the National AI Office and various sectors to evaluate the requirements for national AI readiness.
He added that AI Malaysia will support two key policy frameworks: the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint 2030 (MD 2030) and the Malaysia AI Plan 2026-2030.
MD 2030 aims to boost the digital economy to contribute at least 30 per cent of the gross domestic product by 2030.
Meanwhile, the Malaysia AI Plan 2026-2030 focuses on driving national AI transformation across three pillars: government, the public and industry.
Gobind said Malaysia must ensure its AI transition is inclusive and benefits all segments of society.
He said the government will continue to focus on three core principles - awareness, access and adoption - while prioritising local capabilities and supporting domestic businesses in adopting AI solutions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rohingya refugees housed at KL police headquarters pending relocation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An air of uncertainty hung over the 113 Rohingya refugees temporarily housed at the city police headquarters as they awaited further action after undergoing documentation and identity verification checks.
New Straits Times checks at Dataran Wira found personal belongings and luggage placed along the edges of the square, while the refugees gathered in the central area.
An emotional moment unfolded when a middle-aged female refugee broke down in tears while waiting, prompting individuals believed to be representatives of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to comfort and console her, helping to ease the tense atmosphere.
The atmosphere remained sombre, with the cries of babies echoing across the area. Young children were seen carrying infants, while mothers clutched bags containing essential items such as nappies and diapers.
Police are facilitating the process, including assisting NGOs in conducting health screenings for the refugees as they await confirmation of their next placement.
The refugees were among those who gathered outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Jalan Bukit Petaling yesterday.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks conducted during the documentation process at the police headquarters found that all the refugees possessed valid UNHCR documents.
"A total of 113 refugees, including 110 Rohingya, were transferred to the police headquarters at about 8.50pm yesterday, accompanied by UNHCR representatives.
"The group comprised one Iraqi man, one Somali woman, one Indonesian woman married to a Rohingya refugee, and 110 Rohingya refugees, including 57 adults and 53 children.
"The
Rohingya refugee
s consist of 36 adult men, 21 adult women, 31 boys and 22 girls," he said in a statement.
The group reportedly
arrived in Kuala Lumpur yesterday
on three buses after relocating from their settlement in Penang.
The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority from Myanmar's Rakhine State.
While many are registered with the UNHCR, Malaysia is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol.
As a result, refugees and asylum seekers are not legally recognised under Malaysian law and are generally treated as undocumented migrants.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri polls: PH can retain state, win more seats, says Chow
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Pakatan Harapan can defend its seats in Negri Sembilan and capture additional constituencies, Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said today.
Chow, who recently campaigned in the state, said voter sentiment varied across the areas he visited.
"I cannot comment on the whole of Negri Sembilan because I only visited a few locations. It was a mixed picture.
"There were areas with good support and areas where we faced challenges in mobilising voters," he said after a visit to the MI Equipment facility in Bayan Lepas.
He expressed confidence that the PH election machinery would make full use of the remaining campaigning period.
"I believe the PH team in Negri Sembilan will use the remaining time to defend the seats we held before the dissolution of the state assembly and hopefully win additional seats."
On his visit to the Chennah constituency, where he helped campaign for Anthony Loke, Chow said he went to two locations — one predominantly Malay settlement and the Chinese-majority town of Pekan Titi.
"It reflects what I said earlier. There are areas with good support and areas where more effort is needed."
The Election Commission is aiming for a voter turnout of 72-75 per cent for the 16th Negri Sembilan Election on Saturday.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the target was based on the vibrant campaign atmosphere and the encouraging response from voters.
Early voting is ongoing today,
involving 16,467 eligible
voters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher pleads not guilty to sexually assaulting three male pupils
Article:
BESUT: A teacher pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to four charges of committing physical and non-physical sexual assault against three male pupils since last year.
The accused, Muhammad Izzuddin Mohmad Asari, 31, entered his plea after all charges were read before Judge Ahmad Fadhli Mahmud.
He is accused of committing the offences against pupils aged 12, 13 and 14 at a primary school in the district since last year.
Under the first charge, the accused was alleged to have committed physical sexual assault against a 12-year-old boy at a school cooperative at around 4.30pm in April 2025.
Under the second charge, at the same location, time and date, the accused was alleged to have committed non-physical sexual assault against the same victim by causing the child to view sexual video material.
Both charges were framed under Section 14(d) and Section 15(e) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act, read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act, as the accused holds a position of trust as a teacher.
Under the third charge, Muhammad Izzuddin is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault against another child aged 14 at the same location at around 2.40pm last May.
The charge was brought under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act, which provides for a maximum imprisonment of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Under the fourth charge, the accused is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault against another child aged 13 at the same location between 9.15pm and 10.30pm on June 12.
That charge was also framed under Section 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Akmal Mohd Jazlee prosecuted.
The court allowed the accused to be released on bail of RM15,000 with one surety.
The judge also imposed additional conditions requiring the accused to report to the nearest police station once a month, and prohibited him from interfering with any victim or prosecution witness until the case is concluded.
The court then set Sept 1 for case mention and documents submission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UN chief Guterres sounds out Cyprus sides on prospects for peace talks
Article:
NICOSIA: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres begins a fresh effort on Tuesday to coax Cyprus' rival sides back into peace talks after nearly a decade of deadlock.
His first visit to the island as UN chief comes amid signs the sides may be ready to negotiate again, but they remain divided over the ground rules for talks.
Failure would prolong a dispute that strains ties between Nato allies Greece and Turkiye and weighs on Ankara's relations with the European Union.
Guterres, whose term expires at the end of 2026, is due to meet Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman separately on Tuesday.
The three will hold joint talks on Wednesday in the UN-controlled buffer zone that divides the island.
Cypriot media have reported that the United Nations has assembled a set of ideas aimed at bridging differences between the sides, though UN officials have denied a completed plan exists.
Christodoulides wants to resume negotiations from where talks collapsed in 2017, under a UN-backed model of a bizonal, bicommunal federation.
Erhurman, a elected Turkish Cypriot leader last year, campaigned on exploring a federal settlement, a break from his predecessor's demand for a two-state solution.
However, he says he will not enter another open-ended process without prior agreement on political equality and the rules governing negotiations.
Cyprus was split in a Turkish invasion in 1974 in response to a brief coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece. Britain, Greece and Turkiye are 'guarantor powers' with intervention rights under a treaty giving the former colony independence in 1960.
A power-sharing administration of Greek and Turkish Cypriots crumbled in 1963, and a United Nations peacekeeping force, now one of the oldest peacekeeping operations in the world, was dispatched less than a year later.
It now monitors a 180 km ceasefire line splitting the two sides.
The south is run by an internationally recognised Greek Cypriot government which represents the whole island in the European Union, whose rotating presidency it just held in early 2026.
The north is a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state recognised only by Ankara.
One of the reasons past talks collapsed is strong disagreement on the role Turkiye would play in any post-settlement deal.
Greek Cypriots are against Ankara having any hands-on involvement while Turkish Cypriots say it is essential.
Turkiye publicly advocates two separate states in Cyprus, a position rejected by Greek Cypriots and Greece.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia to unveil new housing policy with 2030 abandoned projects target
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government will launch the third National Housing Policy 2026-2036 on Aug 10, introducing reforms aimed at improving housing affordability and eliminating abandoned housing projects nationwide by 2030.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the new policy is anchored on the principle of ensuring inclusive access to quality and affordable housing while addressing longstanding challenges in the sector.
"The new National Housing Policy will introduce measures to make homes more affordable while addressing the long-standing issues of delayed and abandoned housing projects.
"Under the new policy, we have set a target of ensuring there will be no abandoned housing projects in the country by 2030," he said after launching the Rehda Institute's book, Housing for All, today.
Nga said the target would be supported by reforms under the Madani Housing agenda, including the Housing Integrated Management System, the Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing portal, the electronic sale and purchase agreement (eSPA) system, and scheduled audits under the housing development framework.
He said these initiatives would be consolidated under the National Housing Policy to strengthen governance, improve project delivery and prevent future abandoned projects.
Malaysia's urbanisation rate has risen from 28 per cent in 1970 to 77 per cent in 2025 and is projected to reach 85 per cent by 2040, underscoring the need for more sustainable urban development.
Nga said Malaysia has also achieved 500 million square feet of Green Building Index (GBI)-certified space, reflecting steady progress in promoting sustainable buildings nationwide.
He added that Malaysia is seeking to become president of the UN-Habitat Assembly, reflecting growing international confidence in the country's leadership in sustainable urban development.
To strengthen these efforts, Nga said Malaysia will establish the Cambridge-Malaysia urban platform in collaboration with the University of Cambridge to obtain expert advice on housing, urban planning and climate-resilient infrastructure.
"We are establishing the Cambridge-Malaysia Urban Platform so that the world-renowned University of Cambridge can provide expert advice to our country.
"We also aim to develop Malaysia's own GBI standards in collaboration with Cambridge, setting benchmarks that can serve as a model for other countries.
"This will position Malaysia not only to drive change for our people but also to become a regional leader in delivering quality affordable housing and building sustainable, liveable cities."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia must adopt AI while preserving values, says PM
Article:
CYBERJAYA: Malaysia's push to be an artificial intelligence-driven nation must not come at the expense of ethics, culture and human values.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the country must ensure the adoption of the technology does not widen inequalities or erode its social values.
"We want to reach the heights achieved by developed nations, but at the same time preserve our cultural identity, moral values and religion. This is a new challenge," he said at the launch of AI Malaysia Bhd here today.
Anwar said AI should not be viewed purely from an economic or industrial perspective, as  issues involving ethics, security and its impact on society must also be addressed.
He said Malaysia's graduates must not only meet industry needs, but should also have strong values and a sense of humanity.
He said AI offered significant opportunities but also presented risks, including concerns over security, data governance and the concentration of technological power among major global companies.
"We cannot reject AI because of these risks. We must master this knowledge."
Anwar said Malaysia needed to strengthen AI education from an early stage, including exposing students to AI, improving teacher training and enhancing collaboration between universities and industry.
He also said government agencies must move away from traditional silo-based approaches, as AI adoption required greater cooperation across ministries, academia and the private sector.
"We cannot have an AI nation that is only for government departments but not for the rakyat. An AI nation means government and rakyat."
Anwar said Malaysia's AI journey was only  beginning, but required speed and commitment due to the rapid pace of global technological change.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mercedes-Benz writes off over 700 mn euros on China woes
Article:
FRANKFURT: Premium German carmaker Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday reported falling profit at its car business as it wrote off over 700 million euros due to fierce competition in China.
Though overall net profit for the quarter rose 13.5 per cent to 1.09 billion euros (US$1.24 billion), boosted by its vans and financial services businesses, core earnings at the key cars division fell 26 per cent to 909 million euros, Mercedes said, hit by competition in China.
The figure does not include a non-cash write-down of 704 million euros Mercedes booked in the value of its Chinese investments, indicating it sees lasting trouble ahead in the world's largest car market.
Including the write-down, profit at Mercedes-Benz's car business plummeted almost 94 per cent.
"The Chinese market and customers in China remain of high strategic importance to Mercedes-Benz," the firm said in a statement.
"Intense competition, subdued demand and the portfolio-wide model changeover continued to affect sales," it added.
Premium German carmakers have not been spared the cutthroat Chinese competition that has also hit volume manufacturer Volkswagen.
Porsche on Monday said another 5,000 jobs would go by 2035, bringing total announced job cuts to 9,000, and BMW last month said it would prepare cost-cutting measures after slashing its core profit margin forecast for the year to as low as one percent.
Mercedes-Benz's vehicle deliveries in China – last year already at their lowest level since 2016 – meanwhile fell a further thirty percent in the quarter, the company said.
Citing weakness in China, the carmaker said it now expected sales for the year to shrink up to 7.5 per cent on the 2025 level of 132.2 billion euros, down from a previous forecast of roughly unchanged sales growth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taiwan detains Nvidia worker in chip smuggling probe
Article:
TAIPEI: Prosecutors in Taiwan have detained an Nvidia employee as part of an investigation into the smuggling of the US tech giant's AI chips to China, a source familiar with the case told AFP on Tuesday.
The man was detained after investigators raided his home and workplace on July 24, Keelung District Prosecutors Office said in a statement without mentioning Nvidia.
He is suspected of offences including "the falsification of business documents under the Criminal Code", the prosecutors said in a statement.
The United States restricts exports to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips used to power artificial intelligence systems, designed by industry leader Nvidia.
Officials said in May they were investigating the shipment of "high-end" AI servers made by Nasdaq-listed Super Micro and containing advanced Nvidia chips to China, Macau and Hong Kong, in violation of US export controls.
"This Nvidia employee was identified as a person involved in the case after investigators analysed the relevant evidence following the previous round of searches targeting Super Micro," the source told AFP.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia must raise wages before expanding tax base, says Akmal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia must address the structural issue of low wages before expanding its tax base through measures such as reintroducing a broad-based consumption tax, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
This follows the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD) recommendation that Malaysia consider reintroducing a broad-based consumption tax as part of wider tax reforms to strengthen government revenue.
Akmal said income tax currently covers only about 15 per cent of Malaysia's workforce, highlighting the need to raise income levels before broadening the tax base.
"While we respect the views from the OECD, what is more important is how we broaden our tax income.
"Without higher pay or better wages, any tax introduced may have repercussions on what people consume or what people earn," he said in a press conference at the launch of OECD Economic Surveys: Malaysia 2026 here today.
He said the government's priority was to address the structural issue of wages and household income, as insufficient income levels had limited the ability of more Malaysians to contribute through income taxes.
"Tax expansion is linked to wages because salaries need to be sufficient for people to pay income tax," he said.
Akmal said the government continued to assess more efficient taxation methods, but any future measures must not hinder economic growth.
OECD director of the Country Studies Branch at the Economics Department Dr Luiz de Mello said the organisation respected Malaysia's decision not to prioritise introducing a value-added tax (VAT) at this stage.
He said the OECD had presented a range of policy options on both the revenue and expenditure sides to help Malaysia achieve its fiscal goals.
These include reducing the fiscal deficit to three per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2028 and keeping government debt below 60 per cent of GDP over the longer term.
"Countries consider what they find most appropriate for their specific objectives. We exchange views on options and this is part of our policy dialogue," he said.
According to the OECD Economic Surveys: Malaysia 2026 report, Malaysia has made progress in fiscal consolidation, although further measures will be needed to meet its fiscal targets through 2028.
The report said higher subsidy spending following the conflict in the Middle East had reinforced the need for broader tax reforms, noting that tax revenue, at below 13 per cent of GDP, remained low by international standards.
It said reintroducing a broad-based consumption tax, such as the goods and services tax (GST), would provide a more stable revenue base while aligning Malaysia's tax system with international best practices.
The OECD said targeted cash transfers could help protect lower-income households from the impact of such a tax.
The report also recommended broadening the personal income tax base by streamlining deductions, limiting exemptions and taxing a wider range of capital income, while strengthening tax administration.
It added that large and poorly targeted energy subsidies should be phased out, with the government's newly established social registry supporting a shift towards more targeted assistance.

Title: France and Spain race to contain fires before new heatwave
Article:
NAVALUENGA: Firefighters in France and Spain rushed to contain the worst wildfires in living memory Tuesday, seizing crucial hours before the arrival of another wave of searing temperatures.
Blazes have ripped through vast swathes of woodland in both countries, incinerating properties and forcing the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people – residents and tourists alike.
A large wildfire raging near the French winemaking capital of Bordeaux created a rare pyrocumulonimbus cloud – a phenomenon that can create wind and lightning.
In the southwestern city's surrounding Gironde region, tractors fitted with blades to clear land, pickups towing water tanks and logging trucks sped to join a convoy of fire engines on Monday.
"We want to help... I want nature to stay like it is," said 25-year-old farmer and wood transporter Christopher Bonnefond.
New heatwaves are expected to hit western Europe this week, with searing temperatures returning in France from Tuesday, and in Spain from Wednesday, meteorologists said.
Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said the coming hours would be "absolutely decisive" to tame fires burning west of the capital, Madrid.
In France, the focus was on the blaze near Bordeaux.
Firefighters said Tuesday the fire had not expanded overnight as they managed to tackle several flareups.
French President Emmanuel Macron warned of hard times ahead as he visited a crisis centre in the city on Monday.
"The coming weeks will be tough and we have to hold out," he said.
Over the past six days, the wildfire near Bordeaux has ravaged 42,000 hectares (103,000 acres), forced 220,000 people to flee and destroyed 240 houses.
"Mobilisation is still full and complete, particularly on the eve of a day that is expected to be marked by a significant rise in temperatures and a drop in humidity," the prefect of Gironde said late Monday, describing the situation as "highly unpredictable."
Macron said a smaller fire in the adjoining Landes – which had nonetheless forced the evacuation of more than 30,000 people – was now "contained."
But he warned it "remains virulent and we must be extremely cautious over the next few hours and the coming days."
This was due to the "conditions of climate change in which we will live," he said.
The Landes fire affected 500 hectares in 24 hours, the fire department told AFP.
Some 15,000 people in the region were able to return home as of Monday evening, according to the prefect of Landes.
[[nid:1498849]]
In Spain, where blazes were burning west of Madrid, some 60,000 people have also been evacuated.
At a sports hall just outside Madrid, displaced people sprawled on camp beds, held their heads in their hands and comforted pets.
Maria Angeles Canete fought back tears as she looked around the desolation that used to be her campsite near Navaluenga, west of the capital.
"We lost everything," she said. "We had this campsite, we had another one, and we've lost it all. We have nothing."
The European Union on Monday announced more water-bombing planes were being sent to France, in addition to those already deployed to Spain.
But EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib told AFP that its fleet was increasingly stretched due to fears they may soon be needed elsewhere.
"Extreme conditions are looming for Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, in addition to France, the Iberian Peninsula... where the situation is expected to worsen, including in Portugal starting today," Lahbib said.
The scale of the devastation from the Spanish fires is vast in the worst-affected areas.
Pine trees smouldered with blackened trunks and smoke rose from charred forests, with the burnt-out husks of cars and houses reduced to shells, AFP reporters said.
"You run to save what you can and then you turn to defend," said Karim Benali, 39, a volunteer firefighter on a road near Navaluenga, in Spain.
That country has seen 77,000 hectares – nearly the size of New York City – destroyed.
David Sanchez, a 48-year-old, had just returned home to Cebreros after evacuating at the weekend to find that his small olive and pistachio grove had been consumed.
"Now it's time to clean up and plant again and that's it... and the fire has flared up again down there," he said, surrounded by choking air that stung the eyes and throat.
Some 150,000 hectares of land have burned in Spain and 115,000 hectares in France since the start of this year.
Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called the fires "the most painful expression of a climate emergency."
Spain's weather agency AEMET announced a new heatwave starting Wednesday until the end of the week, with temperatures forecast to hit 42C in the northeast and 39C in the centre.
MeteoFrance also forecast more hot weather of up to 40C from Tuesday with dry wind.

Title: Khairy: BN still in the fight despite tougher Negri Sembilan contest
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Barisan Nasional (BN) still has a chance of winning and forming the Negri Sembilan government despite facing a tougher contest than in Johor, Khairy Jamaluddin said.
The former Umno Youth chief said the remaining three days of campaigning would be crucial for BN candidates to reach as many voters as possible and outline their plans if elected.
"I've been campaigning in Negri Sembilan for the past few days and, honestly, I find the contest there more intense than it was in Johor.
"I hope BN candidates will continue meeting voters and explain what they intend to do as elected representatives," he told reporters after attending the Lepak Pemimpin Ekonomi: Kuasa Penjenamaan, Pengaruh dan Penceritaan forum here today.
He was responding to a question on whether the support from young voters that BN enjoyed in the Johor election could be replicated in Negri Sembilan.
Despite the intense contest, he said BN remained optimistic of securing enough support to form the state government.
"We have a chance, InsyaAllah. We have a chance to win and form the government," he said.
Khairy also acknowledged that the election was expected to be closely fought, with slim majorities likely to determine the outcome in many constituencies.
"This election is expected to be very closely contested, so all of us have to work even harder," he said.

Title: Police chief talks teen down from school building ledge
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Swift intervention by the Kuala Terengganu district police chief today prevented a 14-year-old girl from jumping off the second floor of a religious school building.
Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor spent about 10 minutes persuading the student, who was holding a knife, to abandon her intention before approaching her, taking her by the hand and leading her to safety.
"The victim was then taken to the school's sick bay before being sent to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital for further treatment," he said when contacted.
The student is understood to be receiving treatment at the hospital.
Meanwhile, Kuala Terengganu Fire and Rescue station chief Thoyyibah Taib said the department received an emergency call at 9.33am.
Seven rescuers and a utility vehicle were sent to the scene.
Firefighters found the student behaving aggressively while holding a knife on the second floor of the school building.
Thoyyibah said preliminary information from the school indicated that the student had written about her intention to harm herself in an exercise book.
"Firefighters also helped calm the student and remained on standby until the victim was brought to safety and handed over to medical personnel," she said.

Title: KJ: I'll leave Keluar Sekejap if I return to politics full-time
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Khairy Jamaluddin says he will leave his Keluar Sekejap (KS) podcast if he returns to politics full-time, saying the platform must remain independent and not become a propaganda tool for any political party.
The former Umno Youth chief said KS had built its reputation on balanced discourse and a willingness to criticise all sides, adding that maintaining that credibility would be difficult once he became politically affiliated.
"It is not easy to hide bias once you have chosen a political party.
"That is what has made KS unique from the beginning. It is independent and willing to criticise," he said at a panel discussion at the CTOS SME Biz Day 2026.
Khairy said he had asked KS co-founder Shahril Hamdan to hold him accountable if his views became overly aligned with any political party.
"I told Shahril to go after Umno a little.
"When we record an episode, I tell him that if I start sounding too much like an Umno spokesman, he has to push back.
"He knows the role he has to play. There has to be balance," he said.
Khairy said he remained actively involved in KS, but succession plans were already in place to ensure the podcast could continue without him.
"If I am given the opportunity to contest, win and become an elected representative, then I will stop.
"If I return to politics full-time, I will leave KS," he said of the podcast, which started in 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreigner held at KLIA after abusing staff over flight delay
Article:
SEPANG: An Indonesian man has been arrested after he verbally abused and threatened airline staff and authorities at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1.
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner Ravi Munusamy said the incident occurred about 7pm yesterday when the 25-year-old suspect became upset after the flight he was scheduled to board was delayed by five hours.
"The man then hurled abusive remarks, issued threats and provoked airline staff on duty.
"Security personnel who arrived at the scene to calm the situation brought the man to the Immigration Department office at Terminal 1.
"However, he became aggressive, behaved inappropriately and refused to comply with instructions given by Immigration Department officers on duty," he said in a statement.
Ravi said the suspect was subsequently arrested.
He said investigations found that the suspect had been scheduled to board a flight back to Indonesia at 3pm yesterday.
The suspect was brought before the Sepang Magistrate's Court today and remanded for four days.
The case is being investigated under Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act for using insulting words, Section 188 of the Penal Code for defying an order issued by a civil servant, and Section 294 of the Penal Code for committing obscene acts in public.
Ravi said Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act carries a fine of up to RM100, while Section 188 of the Penal Code provides for imprisonment of up to one month or a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
Section 294 of the Penal Code carries a maximum jail term of three months, a fine, or both.

Title: Bursa Malaysia stays lower at midday with regional tech stock sell-off
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia continued its downtrend to close lower at midday, in line with regional sell-off on tech stocks following US chipmaker Nvidia's talks with OpenAI to help fund a US$250 billion backstop.
At 12.30pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 0.24 of a point to 1,712.85 from yesterday's close of 1,713.09.
The benchmark index opened 1.14 points lower at 1,711.95, before fluctuating between 1,703.83 and 1,713.25 during the morning trading session.
The broader market was negative, with losers outpacing gainers 691 to 252, while 473 counters were unchanged, 1,364 untraded and 36 suspended.
Turnover totalled 1.66 billion shares worth RM1.19 billion.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng told Bernama the recent news on Nvidia has translated into weaker performance of the regional market, with South Korea's KOSPI down 9.72 per cent to 6,098.95 and Japan's Nikkei sliding 3.89 per cent to 62,407.25.
Besides, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index shed 0.11 per cent to 25,178.21, Shanghai's SSE Composite Index was 0.98 per cent weaker to 3,820.52, Singapore's Straits Times Index fell 0.21 per cent to 5,608.54 and Indonesia's IDX Composite Index tumbled 0.04 per cent to 6,183.16
Among heavyweights, Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd fell 13 sen to RM4.62, 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd eased nine sen to RM3.61, Sunway Healthcare Group Bhd and Axiata Group Bhd declined four sen each to RM1.91 and RM1.94, respectively, while IOI Corporation Bhd lost six sen to RM4.39.
Among active stocks, VS Industry Bhd and SNS Network Technology Bhd slipped one sen each to 22 sen and 55 sen, respectively. Dagang NeXchange Bhd decreased two sen to 43 sen, while Tanco Holdings Bhd gained half a sen to 25 sen.
Among the top gainers, Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd advanced 48 sen to RM91.78, Ideal Capital Bhd jumped 25 sen to RM4.00, Tenaga Nasional Bhd strengthened 20 sen to RM14.66, Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd added 18 sen to RM32.00, and KLCC Property Holdings Bhd increased 16 sen to RM8.85.
Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd led the losers, falling RM2.12 to RM43.94, while Batu Kawan Bhd lost 48 sen to RM20.70, Allianz Malaysia Bhd declined 28 sen to RM21.02, and Kelington Group Bhd slipped 24 sen to RM7.97.
Among the broader indices, the FBM Emas Index fell 18.97 points to 12,644.21, the FBMT 100 Index inched down 12.93 points to 12,478.73, and the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased 66.32 points to 17,903.70.
The FBM Emas Shariah Index slipped 30.02 points to 12,456.84, and the FBM ACE Index eased 56.08 points to 4,862.79.
By sector, the Energy Index fell 5.05 points to 764.29, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 1.43 points to 185.41, and the Plantation Index slumped 60.38 points to 9,224.13, but the Financial Services Index gained 5.71 points to 20,246.38.

Title: Myanmar approves death penalty for cyberscam offences
Article:
YANGON: Myanmar's military-backed parliament approved a law on Tuesday that authorises capital punishment for those who detain or violently coerce victims into working in online scam centres, the speaker said.
The "Anti-Online Scam Bill" was passed after MPs approved changes to a draft bill at a combined meeting of the lower and upper houses Tuesday morning in the capital Naypyidaw, Union Parliament Speaker Aung Lin Dwe said during a live television broadcast.
Lower house MP Aye Chan confirmed to AFP that the death sentence remained in the approved version of the law.
"There were not many significant changes to the proposed draft bill after discussions between the lower house and upper house. The important parts of the bill remained the same," Aye Chan said.
Draft legislation published in May said the law included sentences of 10 years to life in prison, as well as capital punishment, for "violence, torture, unlawful arrest and detention, or cruel treatment against another person for the purpose of forcing them to commit online scams."
If committing such an offence caused death, "the death penalty shall be imposed", it said.
The draft bill also featured a maximum sentence of life in prison for those who "run an online scam centre" and those who "commit digital currency scams (crypto scams)."
Internet fraud factories have flourished in war-torn Myanmar, part of Southeast Asia's thriving scam economy, targeting web users worldwide with romance and cryptocurrency investment cons.
The multibillion-dollar black market attracts many willing employees, but repatriated foreigners have also reported being trafficked to sites in Myanmar and tortured by scam centre operators.
The anti-scam law is the first legislation passed by Myanmar's new government, headed by former junta chief Min Aung Hlaing.
He led a 2021 coup in which the military ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and triggered the country's ongoing civil war.
In April, Min Aung Hlaing assumed the role of civilian president after heavily restricted elections that did not include the detained Nobel laureate, Suu Kyi, or her party.
Many analysts describe the military-backed parliament as a rubber-stamp legislature, with pro-military MPs sweeping the vote, which was widely criticised by Western nations and democracy watchdogs as a sham meant to launder the junta's image.
The civil war has seeded instability across Myanmar, creating fertile ground for organised crime groups running transnational scam operations to set up shop in fortified compounds, according to monitors.--AFP

Title: Govt to strengthen AI safeguards against deepfakes, misinformation and scams
Article:
CYBERJAYA: Putrajaya will continue strengthening measures to address threats from the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI), including deepfake technology, the spread of false information and online scams, as Malaysia develops its national AI ecosystem.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said while the government remained committed to expanding AI adoption among the public and industry, security and user trust could not be overlooked.
He said awareness of the risks associated with AI misuse must be enhanced to ensure the technology was utilised responsibly.
"While we want to build an AI ecosystem that is able to empower Malaysians, we also recognise the threats that come with the development of this technology.
"That is why it is important for us to raise awareness about these risks while ensuring that the AI ecosystem being developed is secure and trusted by users," he said after the launch of AI Malaysia Berhad here.
Gobind said among the measures taken by the government was strengthening cybersecurity through the Cyber Security Act 2024, as well as improving enforcement of laws related to digital technology.
He said the government was also strengthening the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and the Office of the Personal Data Protection Commissioner to reduce the risk of data misuse that could lead to online scams.
"When it comes to personal data, we must ensure that it does not fall into the wrong hands as this could lead to various problems, including scams that we are seeing today."
Meanwhile, Gobind said the Digital Ministry was formulating a Digital Trust Strategy, which is expected to be launched by the end of this year.
He said AI Malaysia would play an important role not only in developing the strategy but also in monitoring its implementation to ensure Malaysia's AI development remained secure, responsible and trusted by all stakeholders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HSS Engineers associate wins RM34mil water project contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HSS Engineers Bhd's associate SMHB Sdn Bhd has secured a RM34 million contract to provide consultancy services for the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme (NPWSS), including the sale of excess treated water to Penang.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, HSS Engineers said SMHB had accepted a letter of appointment from Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd for the Lead Design Consultancy and Detailed Design Consultancy 4 services package for the project.
The contract commenced in June and will run for 66 months.
SMHB will provide lead design consultancy services for the NPWSS and detailed design consultancy for the project's water treatment plant.
Its scope of work includes preliminary, pre-final and final designs, tender-stage support and technical support during the construction and defects liability period.
HSS Engineers said the contract is expected to contribute positively to its revenue, earnings and net assets throughout its duration.
The project will be funded through internally generated funds or external borrowings, with no impact on its share capital or shareholding structure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt still in talks over AI software for free youth access programme
Article:
CYBERJAYA: Putrajaya is still in discussions with technology providers on the artificial intelligence (AI) software that will be offered under its free access programme to 100,000 Malaysian youths.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said details of the AI applications involved have yet to be finalised as negotiations were still ongoing.
"We are in the process of discussing. I will make the announcement later when we are sure.
"I do not want to say something and later have a situation where it changes. Give me two weeks to come back to you with that," he told reporters after the launch of AI Malaysia here.
The initiative, announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim,
will provide free subscriptions
to leading AI applications for Malaysians aged between 18 and 30 who complete selected AI-related modules under the Rakyat Digital platform.
Gobind said the programme was part of the government's efforts to encourage AI awareness, access and adoption among Malaysians.
He said the ministry has been focusing on three key areas — awareness, access and adoption — to ensure people understood AI, could use available technology and eventually integrate it into their daily activities.
"Knowing that technology exists is not enough. If there is no access, it creates a problem because people know the technology is available, but cannot use it.
"After that, we need to ensure Malaysians actually use the technology. That is where adoption comes in."
Gobind said the ministry was developing several short and practical modules under the AI Untuk Rakyat programme, including topics such as AI, cybersecurity, cloud technology and other areas linked to digital transformation.
He said participants who completed the modules would receive digital accreditation, with potential rewards or tokens to encourage further use of AI tools.
"Those details are still being worked out — who we are working with and what form the rewards will take."
Gobind added that Malaysian businesses and industries would also be given priority as part of the programme's rollout.
Earlier, Anwar announced that the AI Untuk Rakyat programme would begin on Aug 31 and was expected to benefit 100,000 youths.
He said participants who completed the required courses would receive free access to leading AI software for three months.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perodua expands Sri Lanka export push with Traz, Alza models
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perodua has expanded its presence in Sri Lanka by exporting its latest model Traz, alongside its best-selling multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) Alza.
Perodua president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Zainal Abidin Ahmad said Sri Lanka remains one of the company's largest export markets, with more than 20,000 units sold since 1997.
He said Perodua currently exports completely built-up (CBU) vehicles to six countries, which are Brunei, Fiji, Mauritius, Bangladesh, Papua New Guinea and Sri Lanka.
"We are also planning to export pre-owned vehicles and have expanded this business to Timor Leste this year," he said in a statement.
To mark the launch in Sri Lanka, the first 50 customers will enjoy a special introductory price for the Perodua Traz of 19.95 million Sri Lankan rupees (RM243,000) with additional accessories, or 19.2 million Sri Lankan rupees (RM233,957.23) without them.
Meanwhile, Alza is priced at 19.95 million Sri Lankan rupees (RM243,090).
All prices are inclusive of taxes.
United Motors Lanka PLC group chief executive officer and executive director Chanaka Yatawara said the company has sold nearly 3,000 vehicles since Sri Lanka lifted its vehicle import restrictions in 2025, underscoring strong customer confidence in the Perodua brand.
"With Perodua's proven manufacturing capabilities and United Motors Group's extensive sales and after-sales network, we are confident the Traz and Alza will continue to earn the trust of families and business owners in Sri Lanka," he said.
The Perodua Traz was launched in December 2025 under the tagline 'Engineered Simplicity' and was developed as a user-friendly vehicle tailored to the needs of Malaysian drivers.
The Perodua Alza, introduced in 2022, recorded 19,504 registrations between January and June this year, according to data released by the Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA).

Title: Komtar theme park met safety requirements, says Chow after student's fatal fall
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The operator of the theme park at Komtar, where an 18-year-old student fell to his death from the 68th floor last Friday, complied with all safety requirements and has been allowed to continue operating.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the Fire and Rescue Department confirmed the operator's compliance following
the incident
.
He said the theme park management also informed him that an internal memo was issued to all staff following the fall.
"Following the incident, they issued a memo to all personnel to pay close attention to operations, crowd control and the management of visitors at the facility, and to remain vigilant," he said.
Asked whether closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras were installed at the location where the student fell, Chow declined to comment.
However, he said he was shown part of the CCTV footage of the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's PPI rises 9.2pct in June, highest in 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 9.2 per cent in June 2026, up from 7.8 per cent in the previous month, according to the Statistics Department.
In its latest report, PPI Local Production, June 2026, it said the increase was the highest recorded so far this year.
"Sectoral performance in June 2026 was similar to that of the previous month, with all sectors recording increases.
"The mining sector registered an increase of 29.0 per cent, following a 52.6 per cent rise in May 2026. The double-digit increase was driven by the crude petroleum extraction index, which rose 40.7 per cent," it said.
The department said the agriculture, forestry and fishing sector increased 9.1 per cent, compared with 8.9 per cent in the previous month.
The increase was supported by the fishing and growing of perennial crops indices, which rose 12.5 per cent and 10.8 per cent, respectively.
The manufacturing sector increased 7.2 per cent, up from 3.5 per cent in May 2026, mainly driven by higher prices in the manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products, as well as computer, electronic and optical products, which rose 30.1 per cent and 8.3 per cent, respectively.
Meanwhile, the department said the water supply and electricity and gas supply sectors increased 12.7 per cent and 10.2 per cent, respectively.

Title: Company’s RM19.5m donation to Bersatu was due to project award after Muhyiddin’s minutes, MD says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 —  Construction company Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin said his firm had donated RM19.5 million to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in 2021 and 2022, as he viewed the RM605.2 million government project awarded to his younger brother’s company Sutracom Sdn Bhd as being due to then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s 2021 minutes.
Shahradzi, who will be 44 this year, today clarified why he had followed Malaysia’s Bumiputera contractors’ association’s president Datuk Azman Yusoff’s repeated recommendations starting from around April or May 2021 to donate to Bersatu.
“I’m of the view that Datuk Azman asked me to donate to Bersatu as my brother’s company had obtained the Pulau Indah project on Tan Sri Muhyiddin’s minutes,” he told deputy public prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin at the High Court here.
Later at another point, Shahradzi today told deputy public prosecutor Mahadi Jumaat why he had followed Azman’s recommendation to donate to Bersatu: “I am of the view that, because at that time, the Bersatu president is Tan Sri Muhyiddin, and Yang Amat Berhormat Tan Sri Muhyiddin had minuted my application letter.”
Shahradzi, who is testifying as the 20th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial, was referring to the “minutes” or handwritten note by Muhyiddin in relation to the Pulau Indah highway project.
Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex on July 28, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Previously, Shahradzi had testified that he was informed by Muhyiddin’s alleged close acquaintance Datuk Ayob Ali that then-PM Muhyiddin had written a “minutes” to say he had no objection to the March 2021 application for the project through a pre-qualification tender.
Shahradzi’s brother’s company Sutracom was eventually awarded the project in October 2022.
Shahradzi’s company’s Mamfor’s RM19.5 million donation to Bersatu was done in stages, namely RM10.5 million and RM9 million before and after the project was awarded.
On the donations before the project was awarded, Shahradzi told Mahadi that he had given the money to Bersatu “to help them with the hope that my brother’s company gets that project”.
Asked why he had continued to donate to Bersatu even after August 2021 and when Muhyiddin was no longer the prime minister, Shahradzi told Mahadi: “Because I’m of the view that my brother’s company obtained this project because of YAB Tan Sri Muhyiddin’s minutes when he was prime minister.”
As for Shahradzi’s testimony that Mamfor had given RM19.5 million to Bersatu as it is equivalent to three to four per cent of the RM605.2 million project’s value, he explained that this percentage and how it should be described is up to construction companies’ own interpretation.
“This is the interpretation of the owners of the respective contractor companies whether it is donation or consultancy fee or introduction fee, and that percentage changes according to the interpretation of the respective companies’ owner,” he said.
The RM19.5 million were given to Bersatu in 29 cheques that Shahradzi had personally delivered to Bersatu’s headquarters’ office in multiple occasions over the May 2021 to November 2022 period.
Among other things, Shahradzi told Mahadi that he had forgotten to include covering letters for all the times he had delivered the cheques, and that he did not ask Bersatu for receipts as he did not think it was important since he has records via Mamfor’s bank statement and remittance form copies.
In his witness statement, Shahradzi had said he had complied with Azman’s request to donate to Bersatu, as he “beranggapan” or presumed that Azman’s request was due to Sutracom having obtained a supporting “minutes” from Muhyiddin who was then the PM and also Bersatu president.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik today suggested that this line in the witness statement was actually put in by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), but Shahradzi disagreed and said this was his own words.
Hisyam suggested that the MACC had wanted Shahradzi to say this and that this line with the word “beranggapan” had been repeated 24 times in the witness statement in order to strengthen the case against Muhyddin.
But Shahradzi disagreed with this suggestion.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Today, Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad quizzed Shahradzi over a RM500,000 payment and RM100,000 payment by his company Mamfor to Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd in July 2021.
Shahradzi said the RM500,000 was an advance to Mamfor’s business partner Addeen, but said he did not remember who was Addeen’s managing director.
After being shown banking documents where Azman was the one who opened Addeen’s bank account, Shahradzi agreed with Amer that Mamfor’s payments to Addeen was related to Azman.
Amer remarked that he found it “very suspicious” for Shahradzi to initially say that he did not recall who Addeen’s director was, while Shahradzi explained earlier that he had confirmed the company was linked to Azman after being shown Azman’s identity number in the documents.
Amer suggested that the RM600,000 payment is actually a “suapan” (gratification) or bribe to Azman in return for his help in getting the project for Sutracom, but Shahradzi disagreed.
Shahradzi told Mahadi that Addeen is one of Mamfor’s suppliers and that the RM600,000 payment in July 2021 was an advance fee or mobilisation fee in the construction industry.
While confirming having previously said that Mamfor did not have any project since 2020 until today, Shahradzi clarified that he meant that the company had no government projects or external projects, but said said it still had “internal” projects from his siblings’ companies.
Shahradzi said that this includes Mamfor supplying labour, machines or construction materials to his family’s companies for their projects.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin continues this afternoon.
In this trial, Muhyiddin faces seven charges — four counts of allegedly abusing his position to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for Bersatu (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of money laundering involving funds Bersatu allegedly received from Bukhary Equity.
